Maria V: Heads-up — seeing a spike in client-side stream stalls for /v1/stream/generate in us-west2 starting ~09:12 UTC. 95th pct chunk gap ~1.8s. Server side token emit looks ok. Anyone picking this up? :eyes:
Li: Link to the dashboard? can you paste the per-route token breakdown and kernel_selection heatmap?
Maria V: dashboard: https://dash.redwood/apps/streams?route=/v1/stream/generate
Maria V: quick top-level numbers from the 09:10–09:25 window: token_latency_p50=48ms, p95=220ms, chunk_gap_p95=1.8s, kernel_switch_count=118
Arun: I pulled a raw profile from one of the affected workers. Saw a bunch of kernel fallbacks during short rendezvous windows — sequences ~>512 occasionally triggered fused_attn->matmul fallback because batches arrived fragmented.
Arun: snippet from worker log:
```
[2026-03-18T09:13:02Z] worker=wn-42 kernel_switch: fused_attn -> matmul_fb reason=rendezvous_timeout(200ms) batch_assembled=4 seq_len=640
[2026-03-18T09:13:02Z] worker=wn-42 batching: rendezvous_wait=210ms assembled_tokens=256
```
Li: That rendezvous_timeout of 200ms rings a bell — we pushed a canary for the new batch rendezvous heuristic yesterday to reduce tail latency. Looks like it may be causing smaller, faster batches that break kernel heuristics and force slower kernels.
Li: Also correlating KV cache metrics: kv_hit_rate for this route dropped from ~0.92 -> ~0.48 during the spike window. Eviction_rate also increased. Maybe fragmented requests are creating more unique prefixes so KV pressure rose.
Maria V: Good catch. Can we confirm whether the canary toggled the rendezvous timeout globally or per-route?
Arun: Canary was global on Dedicated pool A (us-west2). I can repro locally by simulating concurrent short prompts — batch rendezvous expires, yields smaller batches that pick non-fused kernels. Kernel selection metric shows degraded throughput when kernel_switch_count > 100 in 5m.
Jules: For triage: suggest 1) rollback rendezvous_timeout to previous value for Dedicated pool A, 2) temporarily bump kv_memcap for the pool, 3) add an observability panel showing per-route kernel_choice x kv_hit_rate correlation. I can add the panel.
Maria V: Quick mitigation patch I can apply now via control plane:
```
redwoodctl set-pool dedicated-A --rendezvous_timeout=400ms --kv_memcap=1.5GB --note="temp rollback after canary"
```
ops-bot: [alert] incident-created id=INC-20260318-44 route=/v1/stream/generate sev=2 trace=tr-9a7b
debug-bot: Collected trace tr-9a7b. Client ack gap timeline attached (uploaded to /internal/traces/tr-9a7b.json).
Li: After the rollback patch, re-run the synthetic workload used in the canary and capture kernel_switch_count + kv_hit_rate for 30m — want to verify stability before re-enabling lower rendezvous.
Arun: Agree. I'll run a targeted perf job (concurrency patterns: many small prompts + occasional long seqs) and post profiles.
Jules: I'll add the dashboard drilldown: per-route kernel_choice heatmap + per-client ack_histogram and an annotation when canary rolled.
Maria V: Action items: I rolled the patch to rendezvous_timeout=400ms (in progress). Arun to run perf job and share profile. Jules to update dashboard. Li to monitor kv_hit_rate and chunk_gap. We'll hold canary until we validate. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
